I think it'd be nice to have a tool that allows you to change a subverses CSS locally only, then commit those changes to the subverse when you're done. It would save on creating a new subverse specifically for testing a CSS. This could take the form of a live preview or something.

Firefox and Chrome both have that feature built-in, don't know about other browsers but in firefox, pressing Shift+F7 (if using windows) opens the console and css editor where you can edit it locally.
This was brought up in IRC earlier. I think this is great, but it wouldn't really help people who don't know how to use the dev tools to that extent, or how to extract their changes specifically.

Or people who use more than one PC or people who aren't able to leave something open. Also, those are both for HTML editing mainly, and debugging, CSS changing, especially when making an entire theme is difficult using inspect element

What I have done is saved a local copy of a few subverses, including ones I don’t own (because they have lots of good example content to apply css to) and then linked in my own stylesheet to it. I just make all of my custom css changes in the stylesheet and refresh the locally saved page. It did require a few minor changes to the site’s actual stylesheet to fix some of the image paths, but it was like a 5 second job.
